entry.reasons: The formula correctly represents average acceleration as defined in EK 1.2.B.3: 'Average acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the interval of time in which that change in velocity occurs.'

CED 1.2.B.3 states: “Average acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the interval of time in which that change in velocity occurs.” The vector formula expresses that relationship, and Topic 1.2 is where it is required. No caution is needed.

a_factual: The formula a_avg = Δv/Δt is correct and matches the CED definition in 1.2.B.3: "Average acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the interval of time in which that change in velocity occurs." The vector notation is consistent with the CED's treatment of velocity and acceleration as vectors (1.1.A.3). b_topic_codes: 1.2 is the topic that first introduces average acceleration (1.2.B.3), and the entry's topic_codes list contains only 1.2, which is correct. c_ced_required: Learning objective 1.2.B, "Describe the average velocity and acceleration of an object," requires students to apply average acceleration. d_caution: The CED states this only verbally in 1.2.B.3 and gives no 'Relevant equation' box for it. The formula is a mathematically equivalent restatement of that definition, so it earns the point and no caution is needed. Null caution is acceptable.
The formula correctly represents the definition of average velocity as displacement divided by the time interval, as specified in Essential Knowledge 1.2.B.2.

Topic 1.2.B.2 requires average velocity: “the displacement of an object divided by the interval of time in which that displacement occurs.” But the formula’s vector notation does not match the CED’s conventions: 1.1.A.4.ii denotes the position vector by r, while 1.2.C.1.i uses x for an individual coordinate. For a vector formula, write displacement using the position vector r, or clarify the alternative notation in a caution.

Topic 1.2 requires average velocity: 1.2.B.2 says it is “the displacement of an object divided by the interval of time.” But the formula does not follow the CED’s symbols. The CED identifies the position vector as r in 1.1.A.4.ii and distinguishes vector velocity dr/dt from x-component velocity dx/dt in 1.2.C.1.i. The entry uses vector x without explaining that departure, and has no caution.
